findings.summary: The criterion-2 integration test calls set_priority directly, so the `athena priority` command's parsing and dispatch in main.rs are never run.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:153 gives a library `Athena` object (`fn athena(&self, script)`), not the binary. The plan says it 'runs set_priority (the same function the command calls)'. A typo in the clap arguments or a dispatch that never calls set_priority would still pass. Fix: Add a clap parse test (Cli::try_parse_from(["athena","priority",<job>,"urgent","--why","x"])) that checks the parsed Command::Priority fields and that an unknown level is rejected. Or run the built binary once in the integration test.

findings.summary: Criterion 2 says the change is 'shown in athena plan and status', but the test checks internal structs, not the rendered output.
findings.evidence: The test asserts plan_entry(...).priority and job_line priority. display.rs may hide the priority or show it only when it is not Normal (the plan notes a Normal comparison there), so 'urgent' could be computed but never displayed. Fix: In the integration test, also render the plan and status (the JSON or text the CLI prints) and assert that 'urgent' appears and the order flips. Add a display test that the urgent level is rendered.

findings.summary: An open question is already answered: the budgets test does not count the generated schema.
findings.evidence: budgets.rs:24-29 composes the reader set from CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and the catalog only. Fix: Remove the budget risk tied to the field doc's length. Keep the doc short for the reader's context, but it cannot break the budgets test. Criterion 6 then passes because reader.md is unchanged, which the plan already states.

findings.summary: The criterion-3 test hand-builds a reading with urgent_reason, so it shows the plumbing, not the reader's judgement.
findings.evidence: The reader is an LLM, so its judgement cannot be unit-tested. Test (c), which checks the parse from ReadingOutput, is the meaningful part. Fix: Use a speed-themed request text (for example, cutting planning stops) and an ordinary one in tests (a) to (c), so the test reads as the acceptance asks.

summary: The plan is sound and puts each change where the fault starts. I read the code to confirm the key facts. In plan.rs (line 43), Priority is derived Ord with High first, so Urgent as the new first variant sorts ahead of High. The old test at plan.rs:644 expects 'urgent' to give Normal and must be updated, as the plan says. Both reading::plan_entry (reading.rs:1514) and status::job_line (status.rs:522) call Priority::from_text on their own, so one shared job_priority helper is the right fix and keeps plan and status agreeing. store.rs JobRecords needs a new field for the records to load, so touching store.rs is justified, as are the other out-of-list files Athena flagged (Reading literals and fixtures). The budgets test (crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs:24-29) composes only CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and the catalog, not the reading schema. A rule kept in an outputs.rs field doc therefore does not count against the 2000-token budget, which settles one of the plan's open questions. The precedence (newest record, then the reader's urgency, then the text) matches 'overriding', and the demotion rationale is good. No athena.toml field is added. The work fits one producer run. All remaining findings are minor: the command's CLI wiring is not exercised end to end, and the plan/status check could use the rendered output.
